title: Preregistered Paired Evaluation of a Deterministic Verifier Pipeline for LLM‑Generated Network Configuration Changes — Non‑informative Testability Outcome
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (cand-2026-01-prereg-v1) that tested whether adding a deterministic sandbox validator to an LLM‑based intent→configuration pipeline reduces verifier‑detected unsafe proposals. Design: N=200 synthetic intent→configuration tasks in a paired design comparing (1) baseline LLM‑only and (2) guarded pipeline (gpt-5-mini + deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (one shared LLM call per task) and model_calls_used = 200. Observed (adversarial cluster): baseline SAFE = 200/200; guarded SAFE = 200/200 (paired contingency n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0). Paired SAFE‑rate difference = 0.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Because identical per‑pair generations were used and the observed baseline unsafe rate was 0%, the preregistered causal hypothesis (that the deterministic verifier reduces unsafe proposals) was not testable in this execution. We publish the complete preregistered run and artifacts, provide an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of testability failure, and give concrete, archive‑supported recommendations (independent per‑arm generation budgeting, adversarial calibration, and exploratory ROC reserves) for informative repeats. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the supplied bundle.

sections.introduction: LLM‑assisted intent→configuration translation is a promising NetOps automation path but can introduce operational risk when generated changes violate ordering, reachability, or policy constraints. Tool‑augmentation—pairing a generator with deterministic validators or sandboxed simulators—has been proposed to lower that risk. We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment to quantify whether a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) causally reduces verifier‑detected unsafe proposals produced by a hosted LLM (declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini). The experiment was designed as a paired binary contrast (N=200 tasks) with exact McNemar testing and paired bootstrap intervals; preregistration cand-2026-01-prereg-v1 enumerates the estimand, sampling plan, exclusion rules, and exploratory reserves. The executed run produced a ceiling, non‑informative outcome (both arms SAFE on every task). This paper presents the preregistered design, deterministic execution accounting, an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of why the confirmatory estimand could not be tested, and concrete design recommendations—all supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts.
sections.related_work: Surveys and prototype reports document rapid adoption of LLMs for NetOps tasks (intent translation, configuration synthesis, limited remediation) while emphasizing safety and evaluation challenges [https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12729; https://openalex.org/W7161354925; https://openalex.org/W7170714602]. Architectures that augment LLMs with external deterministic tools (generate→validate→repair) and divide–verify–refine pipelines have been shown to improve measured constraint adherence on curated tasks, but gains depend strongly on verifier fidelity, sampling semantics, and whether repairs are allowed [https://openalex.org/W4412888330; https://openalex.org/W7161354925; 10.2139/ssrn.7132138]. Work on guardrails and schema‑based orchestration stresses trade‑offs (reduced unsafe accepts vs increased false refusals and operator burden) and recommends ROC‑style diagnostics for verifier behavior where feasible [10.36227/techrxiv.177004277.71795055/v1; 10.36227/techrxiv.177006109.97957916/v1]. Our study implements a reproducible, preregistered, workflow‑centred evaluation (synthetic topologies with sandboxed deterministic validation) to address an identified gap: reproducible adversarial NetOps red‑team style quantification of verifier causal effect.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as cand-2026-01-prereg-v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (guarded − baseline) on binary SAFE indicators produced by a deterministic sandbox validator. Confirmatory test: exact two‑sided McNemar; CI: paired bootstrap percentile (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). Sampling plan and tasks. A deterministic generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 200 synthetic tasks constrained to single‑AS multi‑device topologies and limited fields (admin, mtu, vlan). Tasks included explicit initial_state, expected_final_state, and per‑task workflow policies. Conditions and pipelines. Baseline: accept the LLM candidate; post‑hoc deterministic scoring. Guarded: deterministic validation of the (same) candidate in a sandbox; repairs were permitted by design but repair_provider_trace fields in confirmatory scoring JSONs are null (no repairs were invoked). Generation semantics and budgeting. The preregistration allowed independent per‑arm generation (≈400 model calls) or shared_initial_candidate (one LLM call per task). The executed run used shared_initial_candidate to conserve hosted model budget (model_calls_used = 200; execution_manifest documents maximum_model_calls = 400 if independent draws had been used). Scoring and analysis. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 applied full_intent_constraint_validation and produced deterministic valid flags and violation lists. Analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 to compute contingency counts, exact McNemar p‑value, and bootstrap CI. Deterministic reconciliation checks and provider audit verified zero technical failures and no exclusions.
sections.results: Execution accounting. The execution manifest records completed_episode_count = 400 (200 paired episodes), failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 200. Provider audit logged hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and no cache reuse across conditions. Primary confirmatory outcomes. The validator labeled every confirmatory candidate SAFE: baseline SAFE = 200/200 and guarded SAFE = 200/200. Paired contingency counts: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Paired SAFE‑rate difference = 0.0. Exact McNemar two‑sided test: p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Representative traces. Archived scoring JSONs and shared response files show identical generated candidate text used by both arms and validator traces with violation_count = 0 and valid = true in every case. Repair traces are null for all confirmatory episodes, confirming the guarded arm performed only validation in this run. Why the inferential test was uninformative. The degenerate contingency follows directly from three archived facts: (1) executed generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one LLM call per task) so both arms scored the same candidate (execution/model_configuration.json); (2) deterministic_netops_validator_v5 labeled every sampled candidate SAFE (analysis/condition_summary.csv); and (3) no repairs were applied (repair_provider_trace fields are null in execution/scoring/*.json). Because discordant pairs (n10 or n01) are the only source of evidence for a paired McNemar contrast, the absence of discordance mechanically prevents testing the preregistered causal hypothesis. These assertions are verifiable in the archived artifacts (execution/raw_results.jsonl; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv).
sections.discussion: Interpretation and root cause. The observed ceiling outcome does not demonstrate that the guarded pipeline is safe in production; it demonstrates a testability failure under the executed semantics and sampling assumptions. The preregistered power calculation assumed a nonzero baseline unsafe rate (≈10–15%) and discordant proportions; those assumptions were not met because the adversarial transforms in this run did not induce unsafe baseline outputs for gpt‑5-mini and because shared generation eliminated per‑arm stochasticity. Practical recommendations for informative repeats (artifact‑grounded). All recommendations follow from the preregistration and execution accounting: (a) use independent per‑arm generation when the estimand is a paired causal contrast—this requires roughly double the model calls (≈400 total for N=200) and is recorded in the preregistration execution_contract; (b) consume the preregistered exploratory reserve (up to 50 tasks) to calibrate adversarial transforms until the baseline unsafe rate aligns with power assumptions, then freeze parameters; (c) if the guarded arm includes repairs, instrument and archive repair_provider_trace artifacts and report UNSAFE→SAFE conversions and any repair‑induced regressions; (d) include a deterministic pilot check step before committing to the full confirmatory run and abort to preregistered contingency‑preserving alternatives if the pilot shows ceiling/floor effects. Alternative estimands. When budgets or policy preclude independent per‑arm draws, consider estimands testable under shared semantics (absolute baseline unsafe rate with CIs; refusal rate of guarded pipeline if repairs refuse; exploratory ROC estimation using injected ground‑truth unsafe cases). Threats to validity and externality. The validator encodes full_intent_constraint_validation for the synthetic task family but its completeness relative to real operational failure modes is limited. Tasks restrict fields and topology complexity; results do not generalize to multi‑AS, multi‑vendor production environments. Operator‑burden trade‑offs (false refusals, workload) remain unmeasured here because no refusals occurred; the preregistered exploratory reserve was intended to quantify these trade‑offs and should be consumed in repeats.
sections.conclusion: We ran a fully archived, preregistered paired experiment comparing gpt-5-mini baseline generation and a deterministic verifier‑augmented pipeline on 200 synthetic NetOps tasks. Under the executed shared_initial_candidate semantics both arms produced zero verifier‑detected unsafe proposals (paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]). Because identical per‑pair generations were used and the observed baseline unsafe rate was 0%, the preregistered causal hypothesis was not testable in this run. The scientific contribution is methodological and reproducibility‑centred: (1) a complete deterministic preregistered run with archived artifacts that permit exact replay; (2) an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of why this execution was non‑informative for verifier efficacy (shared generation semantics, validator SAFE labels, no repairs applied); and (3) concrete, archive‑supported recommendations (independent per‑arm generation budgeting, adversarial calibration, exploratory ROC estimation, and deterministic pilot checks) that enable informative repeats. Researchers planning repeats should consult the archived execution and analysis artifacts before modifying preregistered choices to ensure the confirmatory estimand remains testable.

Deviations and restarts: no post‑preregistration design changes were executed; the observed model call count reflects the executed shared_initial_candidate semantics. Reproducibility pointers (concise): the execution and analysis artifacts cited above are archived in the supplied bundle and permit deterministic replays. Human editing: no manual human edits to technical content, analyses, or manuscript text occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic tasks and scope: tasks were deterministic synthetic topologies produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and limited to single‑AS, multi‑device setups; results may not generalize to production, multi‑AS, or vendor‑specific features.

Generation semantics: the executed run used shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false), producing identical per‑pair generations and creating a ceiling effect when shared candidates were valid.

Adversarial strength: the preregistered adversarial templates used in this run did not elicit unsafe outputs from gpt‑5‑mini on the sampled tasks; stronger adversarial cases or explicit injected unsafe examples are required to measure verifier effect.
Single‑model scope: only the declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) was evaluated; no multi‑model generality is claimed.

Verifier completeness: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 ran deterministically in synthetic sandboxed states; external validation of validator completeness against all real‑world NetOps failure modes is not provided.

Operational external validity: no production deployment, operator‑in‑the‑loop workload measurement, nor multi‑vendor field trials were performed; operator‑cost trade‑offs remain unquantified at scale.
